## Several blocks per process and GPU streams (`distribute.blocks_per_process`) {#sec-ch14-bpp}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: a `Mesh` holds $b$ blocks in one process and runs each per-block job on a pool of $b$ worker threads; on a
CUDA device each worker has its own stream, fenced with events against the caller's stream in both directions.
**Switch**: `distribute: blocks_per_process` ($b$). **Default**: $b = 1$, no pool. **Requires**: nothing.
**Order**: n/a. **Defining equation**: @eq-ch14-launch-rank.
:::

With $b > 1$ the blocks of a process advance together: every block-level step (advance, boundaries, exchange,
initialisation) is submitted to the pool as one job and returns when all $b$ blocks have finished it. Within the
process, blocks exchange ghosts by direct copy (@sec-ch14-msgmatch). Remote messages are still posted one block at a
time, under the process-wide mutex. The call order of the mesh-level driver is in @sec-ch01-mesh; this section covers
the threads, streams and events.

### Derivation

None.

### Numerical method

`MeshImpl::reset` clones the block options $b$ times, gives block $\ell$ the rank of @eq-ch14-launch-rank, re-cuts the
coordinate options for that rank and builds the block. It creates the pool only for $b > 1$, on the first block's
device (`MeshImpl::reset`, [`mesh.cpp:225-258`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/mesh.cpp#L225-L258)).

The pool (`BlockWorkerPool`, [`mesh.cpp:47-208`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/mesh.cpp#L47-L208)) works in generations. `submit` stores
the job, bumps the generation and waits until all workers have run it. The first exception thrown by a worker is
re-thrown to the caller. On CUDA the pool takes one stream per worker from the device's stream pool and a done event
per worker. `submit` records an event on the caller's stream before the job, and each worker's stream waits on it.
After the job the caller's stream waits on every worker's done event. So work queued before `submit` is visible to
the workers, and their work is visible after it. Each worker runs its loop under a device guard and, on CUDA, a
stream guard for its own stream (`run_loop`, [`mesh.cpp:134-145`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/mesh.cpp#L134-L145)). `run_block_jobs` calls the job
directly for one block ([`mesh.cpp:265-278`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/mesh.cpp#L265-L278)).

The in-process ghost copy is the other place where streams meet. Each block records an arrival event on its stream
at the rendezvous; the block that performs the copies makes its stream wait on all arrival events, copies, and
records a completion event that every block's stream then waits on (`_prepare_local_exchange`, [`layout.cpp:279-387`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L279-L387)).
The boards of @sec-ch14-msgmatch synchronise the posting stream before they publish a tensor, and the reader
calls `record_stream` on it.

`MeshImpl::forward` runs the advance, then the ghost exchange, as pool jobs. Between them, on the last stage with
the gravity-work fixer on, it sums the five fixer sums of the local blocks in block order on the host and
all-reduces them once per process (`MeshImpl::forward`, [`mesh.cpp:331-363`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/mesh.cpp#L331-L363)). The fixer is the subject of
the gravity-work chapter (@sec-ch06); this section only records where its reduction sits.

| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` `subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block_cuda` | with $6 n^2$ blocks in one process on CUDA, every block's device string is the device and the pool has one stream per block; on CPU the pool has none | exact | integer compare |

| `test_exchange` | three blocks per process: local and remote neighbours both exchanged | value bounds | payloads identify the sender |

The stream checks are in `run` of [`test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp:66-90`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp#L66-L90).
The CUDA case runs only in a CUDA build with a visible device (`snapy_cuda_test_enabled`, @sec-ch14-gpu). Their pass
status at the pin was not run for this chapter.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- PnetCDF output requires $b = 1$ and throws otherwise (@sec-ch14-pnetcdf).
- Block-to-block messages ($x_1$ relays) require $b \le 16$.
- All workers of a pool use the first block's device; blocks of one process cannot be spread over several GPUs.
:::
